sections.1:
This Blueprint Document introduces the Phase 1 Demand Planning scope for Archlin, with the objective of addressing Archlin’s identified pain point of poor inventory planning. Archlin’s enterprise system context is SAP S/$HANA, and the initial implementation focus is Demand Planning. The intent of this section is to establish the business and solution context for Archlin’s demand planning implementation, describe the current planning challenge at a high level, and position the blueprint as the reference for subsequent process, data, integration, and configuration design decisions.

Archlin’s current business challenge is centered on poor inventory planning. Within the Phase 1 scope, the demand planning capability is expected to provide a structured planning foundation that supports improved demand visibility and better alignment of forecast-related planning inputs with downstream supply chain processes. The detailed current-state process, data structures, planning calendars, organizational responsibilities, master data ownership, and integration design are  and will need to be confirmed through Archlin workshops and design validation activities.

For Archlin, Demand Planning is the defined Phase 1 scope. The blueprint therefore focuses on the demand planning processes and related solution design elements needed to support Archlin’s planning transformation. Demand Planning is referenced in the source definitions as DP, and related supply chain planning terminology includes Supply Planning, Inventory Planning, Sales & Operations Planning, Forecast Item, New Product Introduction, End Of Life, Safety Stock, Average Selling Price, Slow-moving and Obsolete inventory, Purchase Order, Purchase Requisition, Stock Transfer Order, Planned Order, Work Order, Capable-To-Promise, and Full Level Pegging. These terms provide a common vocabulary for Archlin’s blueprint discussions where they are applicable to the confirmed Phase 1 design.

The solution direction for Archlin includes establishing demand planning design content that can support forecast item level planning concepts where applicable. Source material describes that New Product Introduction profiles and End of Life profiles can be defined and mapped to the Forecast Item, with demand calculated automatically based on the defined profile. For Archlin, applicability of New Product Introduction and End of Life profile design, the relevant forecast item structure, and the detailed demand calculation behavior are TBD and must be validated against Archlin’s business requirements and available source data.

The implementation approach for Archlin will use this Blueprint Document as the primary design reference for Phase 1 Demand Planning. It will capture confirmed business requirements, process design, planning assumptions, data dependencies, integration considerations with SAP S/$HANA, and configuration decisions as they are validated. Where information is not available in Archlin source documents, the blueprint will explicitly retain TBD or  rather than introducing unsupported assumptions. This approach is intended to keep the Archlin design traceable to confirmed inputs and to provide a controlled basis for configuration, testing, and deployment planning.

The expected business outcome for Archlin is to improve the demand planning foundation that contributes to more effective inventory planning. Because the available Archlin source context identifies poor inventory planning as the key pain point but does not provide quantified baseline metrics, target service levels, inventory reduction goals, forecast accuracy measures, planning cycle times, product hierarchies, site counts, or benefit values, those outcome measures remain TBD. They should be defined and approved with Archlin during the blueprinting and validation phases so that the Phase 1 Demand Planning implementation can be evaluated against agreed business criteria.
sections.1.1:
Archlin is undertaking an enterprise planning improvement initiative focused on addressing poor inventory planning through the implementation of Demand Planning in Phase 1. The current enterprise resource planning environment identified for Archlin is SAP S/$HANA, which will serve as the ERP context for the demand planning design and integration considerations. The company background information, operating footprint, business units, product portfolio, customer segments, geographies, and current planning organization details are .

The Phase 1 scope for Archlin is Demand Planning. The business objective is to establish a more structured demand planning capability that supports improved forecast generation, review, adjustment, and use of demand signals as an input to inventory planning. Within the available source context, the identified pain point for Archlin is poor inventory planning; therefore, the Demand Planning solution is positioned as the initial planning capability to improve the quality, visibility, and usability of demand information before it is consumed by downstream planning processes.

The future-state demand planning capability for Archlin is expected to support automated forecasting that can source and consolidate historical and current sales data and predict future demand for selectable planning periods. The solution capabilities referenced in the source material include statistical forecasting, forecast algorithms, external data imports, forecast adjustments and overrides, forecast reporting, forecast-versus-actual analysis, scenario planning, unit-of-measure conversion, and management of demand hierarchies. These capabilities are relevant to Archlin’s Phase 1 focus because they provide the planning foundation needed to move from less reliable inventory planning inputs toward a more controlled and transparent demand planning process.

For Archlin, the Demand Planning implementation will include the ability to generate forecasts from historical data, apply suitable forecast algorithms, review forecast outputs at different time aggregations, and adjust the forecast where business knowledge indicates that statistical results require refinement. The source material identifies support for daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly forecast analysis; configurable levels such as customer, product, material, plant, period, and hierarchy-based planning; and the ability to manually update forecasts in real time, including modification, cancellation, reset to original values, and application of changes across multiple products with reason codes and comments. These functions will allow Archlin to create a more governed demand planning process with traceability of planner interventions.

The solution context also includes support for forecast reporting, analytics, and insights. For Archlin, this is important because poor inventory planning is typically influenced by the quality and transparency of demand signals, forecast accuracy, and forecast changes over time. The source material identifies reporting needs such as graphical representations of forecasts, forecast-versus-actual reporting, and demand planning reports and analytics. The specific Archlin report layouts, metrics, approval paths, and dashboard requirements are  and will need to be confirmed during implementation design.

Archlin’s Demand Planning process will also benefit from scenario planning capability. The source material describes the ability to create different scenarios, evaluate potential impacts without changing the current forecast, and commit scenario changes back to the parent plan based on an approval business process. In the Archlin context, this capability provides a controlled mechanism to test forecast changes, assess alternative demand assumptions, and support decision-making before demand plan changes are promoted into the operating plan. The specific scenario governance model for Archlin is .

Master data and integration will be important implementation considerations for Archlin because the ERP environment is SAP S/$HANA and the demand planning design depends on the availability and quality of planning master data and transactional history. The source material references the transfer of available master data from SAP to the planning solution, the import of external data, and unit-of-measure conversion to support planning in different units. For Archlin, the exact data objects, interface frequency, ownership, validation rules, and exception-handling approach are .

The expected outcome of Phase 1 for Archlin is the establishment of a Demand Planning capability that improves the reliability of demand inputs used in inventory planning. The implementation will provide a foundation for statistical forecast generation, planner review, consensus-style adjustments, external data incorporation where required, scenario evaluation, forecast reporting, and integration alignment with SAP S/$HANA. Detailed company background, quantified business benefits, implementation milestones, and Archlin-specific operational metrics are .
sections.1.2:
Archlin’s current planning environment is characterised by poor inventory planning, with Phase 1 focused on Demand Planning in the context of Archlin’s SAP S/$HANA ERP landscape. The blueprinting work for Archlin is intended to document the current-state challenges and opportunities, define the future-state demand planning process direction, identify integration and information requirements, and capture expected operational model implications for the planning organisation. The Demand Planning scope includes detailed review of the as-is process, data mapping, forecasting level, consensus demand plan, forecasting accuracy, end-of-life management, and user case finalisation.

Archlin’s Demand Planning future state will replace selected spreadsheet-based and manual planning activities with in-system planning worksheets, including scenario capability. External forecast upload is expected to move from individual manual uploads within the SAP front-end to a bulk upload into Maestro. Archlin’s demand planning forecast process will continue to use the rolling forecast as a basis within Maestro, with product managers able to maintain their own forecasts, perform detailed overwrites for their product groups, and compare against a statistical forecast to refine the plan. The future process also includes automated demand disaggregation within Maestro from monthly to daily buckets at customer, product, and site levels, using historical product mix and a user-selected time period as the basis for disaggregation.

The Phase 1 design for Archlin also requires historical data cleansing to support demand planning accuracy. Product order data, including ShipTo, Product, Customer, and Site information, will require cleansing, with monthly actuals to be maintained once a month. This data foundation is a prerequisite for improving forecast quality, enabling more reliable planning outputs, and supporting a more structured consensus demand planning process. Data mapping and validation are therefore key blueprint activities, alongside definition of planning hierarchy attributes and information requirements.

<IMAGE id="3e496e9ec58f"/>

Archlin’s implementation approach includes structured workshops and validation activities to confirm the demand planning design. Demand Planning workshops cover the current process in detail, forecasting level, consensus demand plan, forecasting accuracy, end-of-life management, future-state process diagrams, integration requirements, data requirements, and operational model changes. The blueprinting activities also include business unit leader engagement to capture current-state challenges and opportunities, reporting workshops to define reporting requirements, master data and integration workshops for data mapping and validation, and validation playbacks of the initial draft plan with business unit leaders.

Operationally, Archlin should expect changes to roles, routines, and user behaviours as planning activities move into Maestro. Sales and Operational Planning processes and related task flows may make individual and group task ownership more visible, with dashboards highlighting late completion and increasing perceived accountability. System access, roles, and responsibilities will need to be decided and assigned for users, with user groups defined to manage access. System training will be required for a wide range of users, with planners expected to require the greatest amount of training and less training anticipated for product managers, BMs, and potentially others such as site managers.

The expected business outcome for Archlin is a more disciplined and data-driven demand planning capability that supports better inventory planning. By moving forecast management, disaggregation, planning worksheets, scenarios, and reporting into Maestro, Archlin will reduce reliance on manual Excel-based processes and improve consistency of planning execution. The solution is also expected to improve visibility of planning tasks, standardise reporting based on user roles, and provide a stronger foundation for downstream supply planning, order management, replenishment, and inventory management processes in later scope areas.

Demand Planning is in Phase 1 scope for Archlin and is intended to address Archlin’s identified pain point of poor inventory planning. The Demand Planning capability will support the creation of a consensus demand plan that can be used as an input to downstream supply and inventory planning activities in SAP S/$HANA.

The source blueprint material defines S&OP consensus demand planning as the process to generate a consensus demand plan. It also describes the demand planning objective as creating an unconstrained consensus demand forecast by combining multiple functional forecast perspectives, with weighting and adjustment performed through a collaborative process within a single planning system. For Archlin, this establishes the target direction for Phase 1 Demand Planning.

Archlin’s current pain point is poor inventory planning. For Archlin, the consensus demand plan will provide the unconstrained demand signal to support planning activities. Specific Archlin role ownership for demand planner inputs, product manager inputs, approval, and sign-off is TBD because the uploaded source documents do not provide Archlin-specific role definitions.

The uploaded source material identifies forecast disaggregation from monthly to daily bucket at ship-to/sold-to level as a demand planning deliverable. It also notes that consensus demand for the first 3 Months can be automatically disaggregated into daily/weekly buckets, if required.

For Archlin, the requirement for monthly-to-daily or monthly-to-weekly disaggregation is TBD. The applicable planning level, including ship-to and sold-to usage, is also TBD because Archlin-specific source data is not available in the uploaded documents.

The uploaded source material identifies a deliverable for roughcut capacity planning and long-term supply planning/inventory planning across a 12 to 18 months horizon, including annual budget and updated forecast examples such as 4+8.

- Long-term supply planning

sections.4.1:
Archlin’s Phase 1 implementation scope is focused on Demand Planning, with the objective of improving poor inventory planning through a structured, repeatable process to generate, evaluate, and align on the monthly Demand Plan for a definable planning period. The current source documentation indicates that the Demand Planning process is intended to create a consensus view of unconstrained demand by combining prepared historical data, statistical forecasting, external forecast inputs, and business review adjustments. For Archlin, this capability will be aligned with SAP S/$HANA as the ERP source for relevant enterprise data, while any solution-specific process calendar, ownership, cadence, process-instance initiation, and process tracking capabilities remain to be confirmed where Archlin-specific source details are not available.

The Demand Planning process for Archlin will begin with data preparation. The Demand Planner defines the Forecast Item at the level required for historical demand aggregation and statistical forecast generation. Historical data is then cleansed before statistical forecasting, with consideration given to demand for which there are no actuals, updates for causals, and adjustments to outliers. Where New Product Introduction or End of Life products are applicable, Phase-In or Phase-Out profiles are defined and added to the Forecast Item. Archlin’s documented input data areas for this process include historical labelling, SKU master data, data hierarchies, Forecast Item information at product, location, and customer level, SoldTo and ShipTo customer information, product status or lifecycle information, and historical sales; where Archlin-specific ownership, data quality rules, or field-level mappings are not provided, these remain .

<IMAGE id="5e785938762f"/>

The statistical forecast generation step will provide Archlin with a system-generated forecast baseline that can be reviewed as part of the monthly demand planning cycle. In addition to the statistical forecast, external forecasts may be uploaded, reviewed, and updated by selecting the applicable Forecast Category. The source documentation states that forecast categories are available by default in the workbook dropdown, that the planner must select the forecast category before uploading the forecast for that category, and that new Forecast Categories can be added only through the solution enhancement process; planners cannot create Forecast Categories independently. For Archlin, the specific forecast categories to be enabled, the source of each external forecast, and the detailed upload governance are .

Consensus Demand Planning for Archlin will support collaborative review of demand volumes, using a system-generated Consensus Demand Plan based on assigned weightings as the starting point. Demand Planners and Product Managers collectively review demand volumes, adjust or override forecasts for selected products when required, and approve the consensus demand or forecast. The final result is published and shared with Supply Planners as the Consensus Demand Plan, representing the unconstrained demand plan. The source process also states that a Demand Review meeting is held once a month, typically in week 2, to align on the aggregated unconstrained Demand Plan, prioritise required decisions, complete decision statements, compare the aggregate business plan against budget, gain visibility of volume assumptions, risks and opportunities, and agree recommendations for Supply Review. The planning horizon referenced for Demand Review is 18-24 months.

<IMAGE id="3b6760f94c01"/>

During the Demand Review preparation, the Demand Planner generates the Statistical Forecast and uploads external forecasts such as Customer Forecast and Manual Forecast where applicable. Based on these inputs, the system provides the Unconstrained Demand Plan using defined ratios. The Demand Review is then conducted with the Product Manager and Business Manager, with any required adjustments or overrides made during the review. The documented output is an agreed unconstrained demand forecast for a rolling 18-24 months, approved by the Product Manager. For Archlin, the exact participants, approval thresholds, exception criteria, and escalation path are .

The approved unconstrained demand output from Archlin’s Demand Planning process will provide the downstream planning signal required for supply evaluation and subsequent S&OP steps. The source process describes that Supply Review compares the Unconstrained Demand Plan from Demand Review with the previous S&OP committed demand plan, reviews inventory position using the Demand Plan together with On-Hand Stock and Firm Supply, and identifies products where supply becomes available later than the due date. It further describes that Demand and Supply balancing may lead to a rebalanced demand and supply plan with alternatives or options to present at the executive S&OP meeting, and that the executive S&OP meeting signs off on the business plan in volume and value for the next 18-24 months. For Phase 1, Archlin’s confirmed scope remains Demand Planning; the implementation will therefore focus on establishing the demand-side process outputs needed to support these downstream planning interactions.

The expected business outcome for Archlin is a more disciplined and transparent Demand Planning process that addresses poor inventory planning by improving the quality, consistency, and reviewability of demand signals before they are used by supply planning and inventory-related processes. By formalising data preparation, statistical forecast generation, external forecast review, consensus planning, and monthly Demand Review outputs, Archlin will have a structured basis for unconstrained demand planning and subsequent supply alignment. Detailed Archlin-specific configuration values, forecast horizons beyond those stated in the source process, integration details with SAP S/$HANA, master data field mappings, and role assignments not explicitly documented remain .
